title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Throughout, mu = {+1,-1}. The page continues the analysis of a finite group Sigma (called E on this page), a non-split central extension of mu x mu by mu. On the previous page it was shown that Sigma is the semidirect product {1, tau_Sigma} . Sigma'' with Sigma'' = Z/4 and tau acting by inversion, so Sigma is isomorphic to D4, the dihedral group of order 8. The privileged involution tau_Sigma maps to (-1,-1).

1. Non-commutativity restated. E is non-abelian exactly when the induced map E_ab -> mu x mu is an isomorphism. Equivalently, the kernel mu (the center of D4) is the commutator subgroup. This is the standard fact that for D4, [D4,D4] = Z(D4) and D4^ab = (Z/2)^2.

2. Pulling the extension back. Let Z^! = M[0] be the profinite (arithmetic) fundamental group in play, presumably an arithmetic orbifold fundamental group of a modular-type object of the 'lacets' set-up, with Galois quotient Gamma_Q. It maps to mu x mu by two characters (eps_3, eps_1). Plausibly these are the characters of Gal(Q(zeta_12)/Q) = (Z/3)* x (Z/4)*; the next page names exactly this identification. Pulling back E along this map gives a central extension S_0^Pi Gamma^! of Z^! by mu.
- Grothendieck asks whether this pull-back splits compatibly with the canonical splitting A already available over Z^o = Ker(Z^! -> mu x mu). He expects that it does not.
- He states that he has proved that the extension S_0^Pi Gamma'' of Z^!'' by mu is non-trivial. He also looks at its restriction to the subgroup Gamma'_Q = Gamma_Q x Gamma_Q^{1 infinity} (the second factor is identified with M(0)'), sitting inside M^S(0) inside M^![0] = Z^!.

3. The Galois part. He proposes to identify the extension induced on Gamma_Q = Gal(Qbar/Q). It is a central extension by mu_2, hence a class c in H^2(Q, mu_2) = Br(Q)[2].
- By construction c is the pull-back of the D4 class along Gamma_Q -> Gal(Q(zeta_12)/Q) = mu x mu. In other words, c is the obstruction to the Galois embedding problem 'embed Q(zeta_12) = Q(i, sqrt(-3)) into a D4-extension'.
- The next page answers c = xi' cup xi'', with xi', xi'' the quadratic characters of Q(sqrt(-3)) and Q(sqrt(3)). That is, c is the quaternion class (-3, 3).

Why this matters for the programme. The two factors mu come from the order-3 and order-4 data, i.e. the elliptic points with fields Q(sqrt(-3)) and Q(i). The question is whether the 'sign' central extension (SL2 versus PSL2 type) splits arithmetically over the Galois group. This feeds the analysis of the 'equation des lacets' (Grothendieck-Teichmuller type relations).
errors: The cohomology group of the class c should be H^2(Spec Q, mu_2), since it is the subgroup Br(Q)[2] of Br(Q); a central extension by mu_2 is an H^2 class. The machine transcription reads H^1.
Likewise, on the next page xi' and xi'' must lie in H^1(Q, mu_2) (quadratic characters), not H^2, since c is their cup product.

Substantive caveat on the follow-up (next page). For any a in Q*, the quaternion class (a) cup (-a) is zero. So c = (-3) cup (3) would be TRIVIAL, contradicting Grothendieck's expectation that c is nonzero.

A direct computation explains the risk. The D4 class in H^2((Z/2)^2, Z/2) is the quadratic form q = x^2 + xy = x(x+y), where x is the factor whose nonzero element lifts to an involution and x+y is the character trivial on the diagonal tau. The pulled-back class is therefore chi_a cup chi_{ab}.
- If x is the Z/3-factor character (field Q(sqrt(-3))), then c = (-3, 3) = 0.
- If x is the Z/4-factor character (field Q(i)), then c = (-1, 3), which is ramified at 2 and 3 and hence nonzero.
So whether c is nonzero depends on which factor Sigma'' maps onto. The formula c = (-3) cup (3), as written, gives 0. Grothendieck himself flags 'sauf erreur en route', and the 'troisieme larron' Q(i) remark suggests he sensed the choice matters.
The hope 'il n'y a pas de scindage' cannot be decided from the Gamma_Q part alone if c = 0. Non-splitting would then have to come from the geometric factor Gamma_Q^{1 infinity}.

ideas.what: D4 as the non-split central extension of (Z/2)^2 by Z/2 whose commutator subgroup equals the kernel; equivalently, E_ab -> mu x mu is an isomorphism
ideas.modern_name: extraspecial / central extensions of elementary abelian 2-groups; quadratic-form description of H^2((Z/2)^2, Z/2)

ideas.what: Class in Br(Q)[2] obtained by pulling back a finite central extension along Gamma_Q -> Gal(Q(zeta_12)/Q), expressed as a cup product of quadratic characters
ideas.modern_name: obstruction to the Galois embedding problem (Witt's criterion for D4 / quaternion embedding problems; quaternion algebra class (a,b))
ideas.usually_credited_to: Witt (1936); Brauer–Hasse–Noether; later Serre's trace-form formula

ideas.what: Whether the arithmetic fundamental group extension by the 'sign' mu splits, compatibly with a canonical splitting over the kernel of the level characters (eps_3, eps_1) attached to the order-3 and order-4 elliptic points
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on the central extension SL2 vs PSL2 / sign obstruction in arithmetic fundamental groups of M_{1,1}; liftability of Galois sections
ideas.usually_credited_to: related themes in Nakamura, Ihara, Matsumoto (Galois action on pi_1 of M_{1,1}, elliptic points and tangential base points)
ideas.where_published: possibly echoes La Longue Marche, but not this specific computation as far as known

missed.claim: Grothendieck identifies the Galois part of the sign extension as the Brauer class c = xi' cup xi'' attached to Q(sqrt(-3)) and Q(sqrt(3)), expecting c to be nonzero. As stated, (-3) cup (3) = (a) cup (-a) = 0, so either the formula or the expectation needs correcting; the correct nonzero candidate would be (-1, 3). This is a concrete, checkable arithmetic statement about whether the canonical mu-extension of the arithmetic modular fundamental group splits over Gamma_Q.
missed.quote: Il serait intéressant d'identifier ... l'extension que Γ_Q y induit, qui correspond : un élément canonique c ∈ H^2(Spec Q, μ_2) ⊂ Br(Q)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a small check for anyone reconstructing the 'lacets' programme: the answer decides whether the Galois part splits. The mathematics itself (embedding-problem obstructions) is classical.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is classical (D4 as a central extension, Brauer classes as embedding obstructions), applied inside Grothendieck's lacets/Teichmuller framework. The one notable point is a likely slip in the follow-up: (-3, 3) = 0 in Br(Q).
transcription_corrections: 'c ∈ H^1(Spec Q, μ_2) ⊂ Br(Q)' should read H^2(Spec Q, μ_2).
On the next page, 'ξ', ξ'' ∈ H^2(Q, μ_2)' should be H^1(Q, μ_2).

'J'ai prouvé [?] que = S_0^Π Γ''' is probably 'J'ai prouvé que S_0^Π Γ'' ... est non triviale, et [aussi] l'extension qu'elle induit sur le sous-groupe ...'; the '=' signs are likely transcription artefacts.
'nous nous sentons [?]' is probably 'nous nous doutons'.
The isomorphism (115) is written E_ab -> μ×μ, where E = Σ of the previous page.
